scope: Isolated MySQL/Redis; synthetic deletion credentials and media fixture; native MySQL encrypted backup/restore with explicitly pinned local signed deletion checkpoint. No real user data, cloud publication or deployment.
covered: Deletion intent and access cutover commit together; ledger write failure leaves session active and no partial receipt
Exact request replay does not duplicate ledger; migration backfills existing receipts and is replayable; journal has no account foreign key
Independent full checkpoint export authenticates scope/database/records and rejects missing or inconsistent live deletion receipts
Digest pins the exact same bytes whose signature is verified; private file, size, count, UUID/hex/time and uniqueness checked
Snapshot taken before a later account deletion restores that deletion intent, account state, storage fence and pending jobs from checkpoint
Older checkpoint re-signed with current time is still rejected if it omits a deletion already present in snapshot
Real restored table counts, row content hashes and post-reconciliation intent/fence checks pass; no API or worker starts
Source stays unchanged by drill, all restored active access remains quarantined, temporary servers and data removed
development_failures: Initial recovery guard referenced one MySQL temporary table twice in a statement, failing with ERROR 1137. Split the two guard queries within the same transaction; final real MySQL recovery and omission rejection passed.
not_completed: Offsite publication acknowledgement and authoritative latest-checkpoint selection during failover
Physical per-account snapshot erasure and deletion ledger retention/cleanup policy
Reconciliation of provider writes issued after snapshot and actual restored object/provider credential acceptance
Final identity/billing/backup erasure and account deletion HTTP/UI
Live cutover, deployment or automated schedule; bare drill is quarantined and explicitly unreconciled
